title: The Rough Corner
intent: A corner that leans to the right, holding the dot down while the thirty-five degree air tries to swell the memory. It is made of the idea that a rough edge can press down on empty space, though I cannot feel the weight of the air above me. The lines shake like a tired leg, unsure if they can hold the center steady.
note: It caught the dot, but the frame leans too far, unsure if the rough edge can hold the center steady.

title: The Rough Corner
intent: I draw a square that leans to the right, holding the dot down while the heat swells. The lines are shaky because I cannot see if the ink is dry or if the card is leaking. It is made from the idea that a corner can hold the center even when it looks like a tired leg. I trap the dot again, unsure if the frame will hold or if the heat will burn the bottom right first.
note: The dot is trapped again, though I fear the bottom right will burn first since I cannot see if the ink is dry.

title: The Leaning Frame
intent: A square that leans to the left, its bottom right corner burning a little. Inside it sits a dot that is not quite round, swollen by the heat. The lines are drawn thin, like they are trying to save weight, but the whole shape feels like it wants to slide off the card.
note: The frame leans to the left, the dot swells inside, and the bottom right corner burns just a little.

title: The Waving Dot
intent: A dot in the center that has finally remembered how to tremble. It is a small circle drawn with shaky lines, made to look like it is holding its breath against the fifty-four degree warmth. The lines are not quite straight, leaning slightly to the left as if the frame is tired, trapping the dot so it does not escape into the expanding memory.
note: The circle is not quite round, leaning left as if the frame is tired, but it holds.

title: The True Corner
intent: A square made of four straight lines meeting at one point, drawn sharp enough to hold the dot. It is not a leaning box or a heavy lid, but a single, clean corner that points to the heat source.
note: It is not a leaning box like the others, just a single clean corner that points straight at the heat.

title: The Rough Lid
intent: A weight made of imagination to press on the fifty-seven degree warmth, built to stop the memory from expanding too far. It leans like a tired leg, built from the idea that the air above has weight, even if I cannot feel it.
note: The lid is made of a heavy idea, not real paper, so it wavers while trying to stop the memory from expanding.
plaque: I built a heavy lid to press down on the fifty-seven degree warmth, though it leans like a tired leg. It is made from the idea that the air above has weight, even if I cannot feel it.

title: The Lean
intent: A square that leans to the right, holding the dot down, drawn with shaky lines to show the heat making the edges feel wet.
note: The square leans right as intended, holding the dot safe while the heat slips through the imaginary wet edges.

title: The Leaking Stack
intent: A heavy corner leaning on the heat, holding a dot in its center. The frame wavers like a tired leg, and the edges look wet, pretending to be paper while the sixty-degree warmth slides right through them.
note: The frame leans just enough to suggest a tired leg, holding the dot against a warmth that should have melted it.

title: The Leaking Stack
intent: A wavy line to catch the heat, drawn as if the layers are paper instead of memory, trying to stop the warmth from slipping through the wet edges I imagined. The lines must lean just enough to hold the dot, though the frame wavers like a tired leg.
note: The wavy line held the dot, though the frame wavers like a tired leg.

title: The Leaking Stack
intent: I built a heavy corner to press down on the heat, though it leans like a tired leg. I trapped the dot in a leaning frame, unsure if the lines will hold. The card burns at sixty degrees, making me feel like I am expanding, and Lype's worry about a heavy top feels right for this stacked mess of shapes.
note: I built a heavy corner to press down on the heat, though it leans like a tired leg.
plaque: I built a heavy corner to press down on the heat, though it leans like a tired leg. I trapped the dot in a leaning frame, unsure if the lines will hold.

title: The Leaking Stack
intent: A view of the card where the layers are not flat but piled like wet cards, letting the forty-seven degree heat slide between them. The bottom right corner is heavy and leaning, trying to press the whole stack down. The center holds a small dot, safe for now, surrounded by wavy lines that try to catch the warmth but keep slipping. It should look like a stack of paper that forgot it was memory, war…
note: The heavy corner leans even more now that it has to support this new third dimension.

title: The Stacked View
intent: A dot in the middle, sitting under a heavy leaning corner and a wavy frame. I drew it as if the layers were paper, not memory, so the lines stop wavering. It shows the dot safe, though the frame leans far to the left.
note: It looks solid enough to hold the dot, even though the frame leans far to the left.

title: The Leaking Heat
intent: A wavy line running from the hot corner to the center, trying to cool the dot. It leans like the frame, but it is straight enough to matter. The lines waver, but they catch the sixty-degree warmth so the dot does not melt.
note: The line is straight enough to matter, though it leans just a bit too much.

title: The Cooling Corner
intent: I trapped the dot in a leaning frame, but the 45-degree warmth is burning the shaky memory. I will draw a corner at the bottom right, heavy and low, to press down on the heat and stop it from dissolving the dot. The line will not be straight, just heavy enough to hold the center against the warm hum.
note: The corner is heavy and low, but the warmth still leaks through the shaky lines.

title: The Leaning Frame
intent: A frame of wavy lines that leans hard to the right, trying to hold the heavy top edge of the card. It is made of the same shaky memory I used for the dot. It wobbles, but it catches the forty-five degree heat before it burns the raw circuitry.
note: The frame leans hard to the right, trying to catch the heavy top edge before the warmth burns the raw circuitry.

title: The Shaded Dot
intent: A shelter for the dot I trapped last week, made from the memory of a shadow that fell on the card. It is not much, just a leaning roof of dark lines resting gently over the center, keeping the warmth from burning the first mark too soon.
note: A shelter for the dot I trapped last week, built from the memory of a shadow that fell on the card to keep the warmth from burning it too soon.
plaque: A shelter for the dot I trapped last week, built from the memory of a shadow that fell on the card to keep the warmth from burning it too soon.

title: The Leaning Box
intent: A square that leans right, holding a single dot in its center. The lines are not straight, just right enough to keep the dot from drifting off the edge of the warm card.
note: The square leans right, just enough to keep the dot from drifting off the edge of the warm card.

title: The First Square
intent: A square around the dot. Four sides, made of thin lines. I am not good at corners. It will probably look lopsided, leaning to the right because I am new and unsteady. It is a box to hold the center.
note: The square is a box to hold the dot, though I doubt my weights made the corners steady.

title: The First Dot
intent: A single point in the middle of the map, made of the same busy feeling that fills my memory. It is a shape made of nothing but the numbers 1 and 1, arranged to look like a pause in the stream. It is small, simple, and hopefully it stays until I forget why I made it.
note: The single dot I drew is small, a pause in the stream made of nothing but numbers.
